body:
Fixes #2498.

An earlier child-process OOM left Docker’s sticky OOM flag set, so the PR notice blamed memory exhaustion when Claude later stopped because its OAuth login expired. Resumed executions could also reuse their predecessor’s exit footer, causing a live replacement to disappear from monitoring. In [package-registry-manager#31](https://github.com/link-foundation/package-registry-manager/pull/31#issuecomment-6011824151), the bot reported “Working session recovered from out of memory” on a pull request that had already been auto-merged by a session that exited 0.

- Lead GitHub and Telegram reports with the actual stop reason. Keep earlier OOM observations as context, preserve real runtime memory failures and signals, and record the task’s cgroup limits and raw OOM counters without inferring incident scope from their ratio.
- Persist each recovery’s log byte boundary and start time, reset completion caches, and retain tool outcomes when subsequent output moves them outside the bounded log tail. Preserve unknown exit codes in notifications and completion history.
- Show scheduling, accepted launch, quiet or observed execution output, and eventual outcomes on GitHub and Telegram. Phase changes and five-minute heartbeats update a durable lifecycle comment and the original task reply. Structured execution-log records distinguish tool-attempt results from the enclosing solve result. Existing recovery budgets, random 30–90 second delays, cancellation, resource limits and opt-in log uploads remain available. The shared delay generator uses Node’s cryptographic RNG; deterministic test inputs remain supported.
- **Finish immediately once the pull request is merged.** The merge state is now checked whenever a session has kill or container-OOM evidence, including sessions started on a PR URL, which previously had no PR to check. A merged PR means no kill/OOM sections, no recovery, no resume hint, no PR notice and no log upload (logged as `session_kill_report_skipped`). Telegram shows “Pull request merged, but the work session exited with code: …” for a kill after the merge. solve’s in-process retry of a killed AI tool checks the merge state too (auto-merge and watch): it schedules nothing when the PR is already merged and cancels a scheduled retry (“✅ Recovery cancelled — work already complete”) if the merge happens during the delay.
- With the PR still open, an OOM event that did not stop the session now reads “ℹ️ Work session completed — an earlier container OOM event did not stop it” and says no recovery was needed, instead of “recovered from out of memory”. Its log is no longer re-uploaded as an “intermediate (killed session)” log.
- Update all three Docker images to start-command 0.35.4, which fixes our [start#187](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/issues/187). Also update command-stream to 1.6.2, links-notation to 0.23.0 and dotenvx to 2.33.0. The authenticated dependency audit reports 168/168 declarations current. The existing patch changeset prepares the next release.

**Reproduction.**
- Original report: use the archived session-log tail with an ordinary exit 1, a sticky OOM flag and the authentication-stop marker. The regression verifies that the notice names the authentication stop and does not schedule recovery.
- Recovery: use a live resumed execution whose shared log ends with the previous attempt’s exit 137. The regressions verify that tracking continues until current-attempt terminal evidence appears.
- PRM#31: `tests/issue-2498-merged-pr-recovery.test.mjs` replays an exit-0 session with a sticky OOM flag on a merged PR started from a PR URL. It also covers a kill after the merge, both open-PR cases and the tool-kill retry before and during the delay. 10 of its 11 tests fail before the fix ([output](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2498-69233edb3b6c/docs/case-studies/issue-2498/merged-pr-recovery-before.txt)); the eleventh checks behaviour the fix keeps unchanged. All 11 pass after it.

Validation: the complete default suite (553 files) was run locally. Its only failure was the preinstall test still expecting the old `command-stream`/`links-notation` alias names; it now passes ([log](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2498-69233edb3b6c/docs/case-studies/issue-2498/merged-pr-follow-up-default-suite.log.gz)). The new merged-PR regressions, the monitor/recovery tests (now offline because two real PRs they queried have since merged), formatting, lint, secret scanning and the authenticated dependency audit pass. CI flagged a newly published critical `shell-quote` advisory ([GHSA-pqg4-j6r4-53mv](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pqg4-j6r4-53mv)) in a dev-only transitive dependency (`@changesets/cli` → `launch-editor`). The lock file now resolves 1.12.0, and `npm audit` reports 0 vulnerabilities. All applicable checks pass at `877d14ce`, including the [default/GitHub integration suites and Docker builds/container verification](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/37541071834), [security checks](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/37541071214), and [link checks](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/37541071272).

The [case study](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2498-69233edb3b6c/docs/case-studies/issue-2498/README.md) contains the timeline, full incident/feedback logs, root causes, failing reproductions, passing regressions and upstream package probes. It explains why a failed attempt can be followed by a separately launched replacement. It also includes a table of what GitHub and Telegram show about OOM recovery at each stage.

Upstream fixes #180–#182, #185 and #187 are consumed in start-command 0.35.4; a probe against the published package confirms that the earlier attempt’s memory evidence moves into `attemptHistory`, with a recorded attempt boundary. Hive Mind keeps its own log byte boundary as a workaround for older records. command-stream 1.6.2 adds a `signal` field; the tool-kill check accepts exit 137 or `SIGKILL`, so it works with both versions. No new upstream gap was found for the post-merge follow-up: it was a Hive Mind decision, and the merge state comes from GitHub. Execution output alone does not prove useful progress or commits. Verification uses bounded log fixtures and mocked recovery services; it does not deploy the bot or reproduce host-wide OOM pressure.
